subject: Satellite edge cluster: node pool mix, local NVMe cache, and cold-tier storage plan
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <s.torres@heliogrid.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@corpinfra.io>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Satellite edge cluster: node pool mix, local NVMe cache, and cold-tier storage plan

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for last week's intake. Attached is a first-pass proposal for the small ("satellite") clusters you plan to deploy at five retail sites. High level summary up front:

- Cluster footprint per site: 3 physical hosts (2x worker + 1x control-plane/edge-proxy), 384GB RAM per worker, 16 vCPU, local NVMe on each worker intended for KV/cache and ephemeral model artifacts.
- Node pools: cpu-constrained pool for API pods; memory-optimized pool for model runtime; infra pool for logging/monitoring/egress proxies (tainted + limited scale).
- Storage: local NVMe for prefix/KV cache (fast ephemeral), a small fast persistent pool (10TB) backed by local NVMe+LVM for low-latency PVs, and a cold-tier exported to central NFS/Ceph over encrypted L3 for backups and longer-term storage.
- Networking: VPC with dedicated transit VPC for control-plane egress, BGP peering for site-to-core connectivity, MTU 9000 where NVMeoF expected; otherwise 1500. Firewall rules limited to known Redwood control-plane IPs and your aggregator.
- Compliance: KMS integration required (customer HSM or AWS KMS via transit VPC) and audit logs forwarded to central SIEM.

Key questions for you before we lock the runbook:
1) Do we have an on-site NTP/time-sync source or should we configure NTP to your central time pool?
2) Will the site network allow MTU 9000 for NVMe-backed replication, or should we assume 1500 only?
3) Do you plan to host an on-site container registry mirror (recommended for airgapped/slow links)?

Action items: I attached satellite-sizing-v1.xlsx and a quick network sketch (network-sketch-siteA.pdf). Can you confirm answers to the three questions above and share any standard firewall ACL templates you need us to follow? Once we have that we’ll produce a final storage-class YAML + nodepool definitions for your infra team.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Satellite edge cluster: node pool mix, local NVMe cache, and cold-tier storage plan

Thanks Sofia — this looks close to what we expected. A few clarifications: 

- NTP: we have a GPS-backed time server at each site; you can configure cluster nodes to point to it.
- MTU: unfortunately our existing switches are fixed at 1500; no jumbo frames for the next 18 months.
- Registry mirror: yes, we will run a lightweight registry mirror on an appliance in the aggregator; we’ll provide credentials.

Storage question: for the cold-tier, you mention Ceph over encrypted L3. We currently have a central NetApp NFS cluster and a NetApp team that prefers NFS mounts over iSCSI. Will that be OK, or do you recommend Ceph/iSCSI for performance?

Also — what will the snapshot cadence be for persistent volumes that hold model metadata? We need retention policy suggestions for legal.

Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Infrastructure — HelioGrid Systems
s.torres@heliogrid.com
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Satellite edge cluster: node pool mix, local NVMe cache, and cold-tier storage plan

Team — forwarding Sam's answers. He confirmed NTP and registry mirror; MTU stuck at 1500 and central storage is NetApp NFS. He asked for guidance on snapshot cadence and whether NFS is acceptable for the cold-tier. Thoughts and concrete knobs we should hand back to the customer: storage-class examples, eviction thresholds, and nodepool taints/tolerations.

My quick recommendations:
- Accept NetApp NFS as the cold-tier. Use a Ceph alternative only if they need block semantics for latency-sensitive stateful sets. For our workloads (model metadata + artifacts) NFS is acceptable provided we limit IOPS and use a local cache tier for hot reads.
- Storage classes: define three SCs - local-ephemeral (hostPath/LVM with reclaim policy Delete, no replication), fast-local (LV-backed EXT4/XFS with fsGroup + encryption at mount via dm-crypt, reclaim Retain or Delete per site preference), and cold-nfs (NFS with mountOptions rw,noatime,nodiratime, and snapshot policy at central NetApp). Attach sample YAML (csi-storage-class-examples.yaml).
- Snapshot cadence suggestion: for model metadata PVs: hourly delta snapshots for first 24 hours, then daily snapshots for 14 days, then weekly for 12 weeks (customer legal can shorten/lengthen). Total retention approx 90 days by default. For logs, shorter retention (14–30 days).
- Kubelet eviction thresholds: set node.kubelet.evictionHard to memory.available<200Mi,nodefs.available<5% and evictionSoft at 300Mi for memory to give pods a chance to gracefully exit.
- Nodepool layout:
  * nodepool-api (cpu, replicas 3, taint: NoSchedule=infra:No)
  * nodepool-model (mem & cpu, replicas 2 per site, tolerations for gpu:false and label model-runtime=true)
  * nodepool-infra (1 replica, tainted infra=true:NoSchedule, runs fluenet/metricbeat/egress-proxy)

Networking: since MTU is 1500, plan for NVMe caches to be local-only (no NVMeoF replication). All replication/backups go over aggregated WAN to NetApp; recommend encrypting with IPsec between site and aggregator.

Security/KMS: integrate with customer HSM for disk encryption and ensure CSI driver supports provider's KMS; otherwise use transit KMS with envelope encryption.

Can you confirm and I’ll prepare a single-page runbook and a firewall rule checklist to send to HelioGrid?

— Irene (on behalf of team)
Irene Choi
Principal Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Hi Sam / Elena —

Thanks for the quick answers. We reviewed with our on-prem team and the proposals below are the actionable plan we recommend. We’re keeping changes minimal to fit your existing NetApp + 1500-MTU constraints.

Short plan (deliverables):
1) Runbook PDF with final nodepool specs, CSI storage-class YAML, kubelet eviction settings, and backup cadence. (deliverable by 2026-08-06)
2) Firewall/ACL checklist for your network team (ports/IPs for Redwood control-plane + registry mirror + NTP + NetApp exports).
3) On-site readiness call to validate physical inventory and provide the image registry mirror config (30–45 min). Proposed slots: Thu 2026-08-05 09:00–09:45 PT or Fri 2026-08-06 11:00–11:45 PT — pick one and we’ll send calendar invite.

Notes and specific config hints you can hand to your infra team:
- Storage classes: attach csi-storage-class-examples.yaml (fast-local, cold-nfs, local-ephemeral). We will template encryption-at-rest via dm-crypt for fast-local.
- Snapshot policy: hourly -> 24h, daily -> 14d, weekly -> 12w (defaults). Provide retention exception form if legal needs >90d.
- KMS: If HelioGrid can expose a KMIP endpoint to the cluster, we will configure CSI to call it. Otherwise we’ll use envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KMS keys over the transit VPC.
- Firewall minimum: allow HTTPS/443 to registry mirror host, TCP 2049 to NetApp NFS from aggregator only, SSH from your ops jump host, and control-plane ports to our control-plane CIDR. Full checklist in the runbook.

Next steps: please confirm the meeting slot (Thu 8/5 09:00 PT preferred) and upload your NetApp export names + registry mirror credentials to the secure Drive link below. Once we get that we’ll produce the runbook and attach the YAML.

Best,
Sofia
